findings.title: Authenticated command execution via MCP stdio test endpoints (GHSA-v4p8-mg3p-g94g, CVE-2026-42271)
findings.summary_md: Maintainer-published LiteLLM advisory for CVE-2026-42271, rated High 8.7 (CVSS v4), affecting litellm >=1.74.2 and <1.83.7. The POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list endpoints spawned attacker-supplied commands as a subprocess with only a proxy API key required and no role check, so any low-privilege key holder could run commands on the proxy host. Fixed in 1.83.7 by requiring the PROXY_ADMIN role; the stated workaround is to block both endpoints at the reverse proxy.

findings.title: Disclosing the BADHOST Vulnerability in Starlette
findings.summary_md: OSTIF published expanded details on CVE-2026-48710, a host-header input-sanitization flaw in Starlette that bypasses authentication with a single character. OSTIF warned that slow uptake of patched Starlette versions and exposed live services were a serious concern, and that the bug hits a wide swath of Python LLM infrastructure including FastAPI, LiteLLM, vLLM, most OpenAI shim proxies, MCP servers, agent harnesses, and model-management UIs.

findings.title: CVE-2026-42271 Chained with CVE-2026-48710: LiteLLM Unauthenticated RCE
findings.summary_md: Horizon3 researchers validated that CVE-2026-42271, originally disclosed as authenticated command injection in LiteLLM's MCP test endpoints, can be chained with CVE-2026-48710 (Starlette BadHost bypass, dependency tree including Starlette 1.0.0 or older) for unauthenticated remote code execution on LiteLLM 1.74.2 through 1.83.6, assessing the chain as CVSS 10.0. Their timeline records the April 20, 2026 disclosure of CVE-2026-42271, the May 8, 2026 fix in LiteLLM 1.83.7, the May 26, 2026 BadHost disclosure, and their June 1, 2026 validation. Remediation: LiteLLM 1.83.7 or later, Starlette 1.0.1 or later, block the MCP test endpoints, and rotate proxy-stored credentials.

findings.title: Unauthenticated RCE via /configs path-suffix auth-filter bypass (GHSA-2q47-568g-9h4f, CVE-2026-53576)
findings.summary_md: Kestra's Critical 10.0 advisory for CVE-2026-53576: the REST API authentication filter treated any request path ending in /configs as the public instance-config endpoint, so an anonymous caller could create a flow carrying a Shell task and trigger it, executing as root inside the Kestra container and pivoting through the /var/run/docker.sock mounted by the official docker-compose file. Affects Kestra OSS up to 1.3.20; patched in 1.3.21 and 1.0.45. Published June 3, 2026, crediting reporter Jan Kahmen of turingpoint.

findings.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2026-42271, the BerriAI LiteLLM command injection vulnerability, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 8, 2026 based on evidence of active exploitation, alongside CVE-2026-50751, a Check Point Security Gateway improper authentication vulnerability. Federal agencies were given the standard KEV remediation deadline to patch or discontinue use.
